context.body: The unit carries the prior priesthood argument forward without repeating Melchizedek’s name or the oath.
context.label: Melchizedek is no longer named

observations.body: Hebrews identifies a seated high priest who serves in the true heavenly tabernacle and mediates a better covenant founded on better promises.
observations.label: The argument names its main point

observations.body: The passage moves from the priest’s seat and sanctuary to the need for an offering, the earthly copy, and the superiority of ministry and covenant.
observations.label: Priesthood becomes ministry

payload.posture: Inspect Hebrews 8:1–6 as a bounded source before following its claims into another passage.
payload.tension: The passage calls the earthly service a copy and shadow but does not treat it as unreal or explain every detail of the heavenly sanctuary.
payload.title: The high priest ministers at the true tabernacle
